title: 游园不值
titleEn: Visiting a Garden, Finding No One Home
author: 叶绍翁
intro: The poet knocks at a friend’s garden gate; nobody answers. A little disappointing — until he looks up and sees one branch of red apricot blossom reaching over the wall. Spring can’t be locked in.
analysis: 题目“游园不值”的意思是：去游园，却没遇到主人，没能进去。前两句写诗人去朋友的花园，大概是主人心疼门前的青苔，怕被木鞋的鞋齿踩坏，所以轻轻敲柴门，敲了很久也没人开。本来有点扫兴，可是后两句一下子转了：满园的春色是关不住的，一枝红杏已经伸出墙来。诗人虽然没进园子，却从这一枝红杏想象到了园里满满的春天，失望变成了惊喜。这种“以小见大”（从一个小东西看到整体）的写法，让短短四句很有画面感。“春色满园关不住，一枝红杏出墙来”今天也比喻美好的、新生的东西挡也挡不住。
analysisEn: The title means “visiting a garden but not getting in” — the owner wasn’t home. In the first two lines the poet arrives at a friend’s garden. Perhaps, he jokes, the owner is protecting the green moss by the gate from the teeth of visitors’ wooden clogs, because he knocks gently on the brushwood gate for a long time and no one opens it. It is a small letdown. Then the last two lines turn everything around: a whole garden of spring cannot be shut in — one branch of red apricot blossom has pushed out over the wall. He never gets inside, but from that single branch he can picture the spring filling the garden, and disappointment becomes delight. Seeing the whole through one small detail gives these four lines a vivid, cheerful picture. The last couplet is still quoted to mean that something fresh and full of life cannot be held back.
background: Ye Shaoweng (dates unknown) lived in the Southern Song around the early 13th century and spent much of his life in seclusion near West Lake in Hangzhou. Little else is known about him; this poem is by far his most famous.
pronunciation: 应怜 yīng lián（应该，不读 yìng）。屐齿 jī chǐ。柴扉 chái fēi。“不值”：值 指遇到，读 zhí。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材文本。异文：“小扣”一作“小叩”。此诗由陆游《马上作》“杨柳不遮春色断，一枝红杏出墙头”化出，后来居上。

lines.py: yīng lián jī chǐ yìn cāng tái
lines.lit: Probably he cares that clog teeth would print the green moss,
lines.en: Perhaps he fears my wooden clogs would mark his moss —

lines.py: xiǎo kòu chái fēi jiǔ bù kāi
lines.lit: gently I knock at the brushwood gate; for a long time it does not open.
lines.en: I tap and tap at the wooden gate, but no one comes.

lines.py: chūn sè mǎn yuán guān bù zhù
lines.lit: Spring colour fills the garden and cannot be shut in:
lines.en: Yet a garden full of spring cannot be locked away:

lines.py: yī zhī hóng xìng chū qiáng lái
lines.lit: one branch of red apricot comes out over the wall.
lines.en: one branch of red apricot blossom leans out over the wall.

words.note: 值：遇到。古义，和今天“值钱”“不值得”完全不同。
古义“爱惜”；现代汉语多指“可怜”。

words.en: the wooden teeth under old clogs
words.note: 屐：木头鞋，鞋底有齿，今天日本的木屐还有。
扣：同“叩”，敲。现代说“轻轻敲门”。

words.en: the colours of spring; springtime scenery
(today, colloquial) a wife having an affair
words.note: 注意：今天口语里“红杏出墙”常比喻妻子有外遇，和这首诗原意无关，日常说话要小心使用。

imagery.name: 杏花
imagery.zh: 伸出墙外的一枝红杏，让人看到整个园子的春天，代表关不住的生机。
imagery.en: One branch of apricot over the wall reveals the whole spring garden — life that can’t be held in.

imagery.name: 苔
imagery.zh: 门前长满青苔，说明这里少有人来，主人生活清静。
imagery.en: Moss by the gate shows few visitors come; the owner lives a quiet life.

imagery.name: 柴扉
imagery.zh: 简朴的柴门，关着不开，是“不值”的原因，也让后面的惊喜更突出。
imagery.en: The plain wooden gate stays shut — the disappointment that makes the surprise sweeter.
